forces.title: Strait of Hormuz closure causes crude/LPG supply disruption
forces.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz since February 2026 has severely disrupted crude oil and LPG supply chains to India. This chokepoint, through which historically half of India's crude imports and a significant portion of its LPG imports pass, led to a rapid shift in crude sourcing away from traditional West Asian suppliers towards Russia and UAE (non-Hormuz routes), and a near halving of LPG imports. This event highlights the extreme vulnerability of midstream infrastructure, including crude/product pipelines, storage terminals, and LNG shipping vessels, to geopolitical events and chokepoint risks, leading to higher procurement costs and operational challenges.
forces.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

forces.title: Diversification of crude oil import sources and routes
forces.description: India has demonstrated significant agility in diversifying its crude oil import basket following geopolitical disruptions. The share of Russian crude in India's imports dramatically increased from negligible levels to 48% by June 2026, directly substituting Iraqi and Saudi grades that transit the Strait of Hormuz. Similarly, LPG sourcing shifted to the US Gulf Coast. This structural pivot towards non-Hormuz-dependent routes and suppliers from diverse geographies enhances energy security and reduces chokepoint risk for midstream operations, improving the resilience of pipeline networks, storage terminals, and shipping logistics.
forces.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

forces.title: Elevated LPG under-recoveries strain OMC profitability
forces.description: Unprecedented disruptions to the global LPG supply chain, primarily due to the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz closure, led to a surge in LPG procurement costs. Despite government compensation and retail price hikes, OMCs incurred significant LPG under-recoveries (Rs 13,700 crore in Q1FY27). While expected to moderate, these under-recoveries continue to burden OMCs, impacting their overall profitability and potentially limiting investment capacity in midstream LPG infrastructure. The higher landed cost due to longer shipping routes from diversified sources adds persistent pressure.
forces.source_title: OMCs LPG Under Recovery Expected to Fall ~40% Q-o-Q in Q2FY27

forces.title: Increased cost of imported LNG for fertilizer production
forces.description: India's high dependence on imported LNG, primarily from the Gulf and transiting the Strait of Hormuz, exposes its fertilizer sector to external energy shocks. Geopolitical tensions causing LNG flow disruptions have led to surging domestic LNG prices, strained reserves, and distribution delays. Since natural gas is a critical feedstock for ammonia (and thus fertilizer) production, these disruptions directly increase input costs for fertilizer plants. This higher cost for a significant end-user of gas transmission negatively impacts the midstream sector's pricing power and demand stability from this key industrial segment.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Potential US tariffs on Indian exports for Russian oil purchases
forces.description: The proposed US Graham Act, if enacted and strictly enforced, could impose up to 100% tariffs on Indian exports as a top buyer of Russian oil. While the direct benefit of Russian oil discounts has narrowed for India, a forced disorderly exit from Russian crude, especially if the Strait of Hormuz remains shut, would significantly tighten global crude supply and push Brent prices above $100/bbl. This scenario poses a severe risk to India's energy security and economy, leading to potential demand destruction for refined products and crude imports, which would directly impact midstream throughput and profitability.
forces.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

forces.title: Higher domestic natural gas production boosts midstream volumes
forces.description: Increased domestic natural gas production directly leads to a greater volume of gas available for gathering, processing, and transmission through pipeline networks and storage facilities. This higher supply boosts demand for midstream services, enhancing throughput and revenue for gas transmission networks and related infrastructure. This is a significant tailwind for the sector, improving capacity utilization, operational efficiency, and overall business prospects as domestic supply is channeled through these assets.

forces.title: Increased petroleum refinery output drives product pipeline demand
forces.description: Increased petroleum refinery output directly translates to a greater volume of refined products that require transportation via pipelines and storage. This enhances demand for midstream logistics, specifically product pipelines and storage terminals, boosting their utilization and revenue. As India's refining capacity expands and product demand grows, this creates a sustained tailwind for the midstream sector, ensuring consistent volumes through its networks.

forces.title: Rising petroleum imports necessitate increased midstream handling
forces.description: Higher volumes of crude oil and petroleum product imports into India directly necessitate increased handling at ports, transportation through pipelines, and storage in terminals. This phenomenon directly benefits the midstream infrastructure by driving higher throughput and utilization of existing assets. This is a strong tailwind as India's energy demand continues to outpace domestic production, ensuring a steady flow of commodities through the midstream network for processing and distribution.

forces.title: Growing petroleum consumption boosts transport and storage demand
forces.description: Rising total petroleum consumption in India directly translates to higher volumes of refined products needing transportation and storage across the country. This robust demand boosts midstream services, including pipeline networks and storage terminals, driving their utilization and revenue. As India's economy grows and energy demand increases, particularly in transport and industrial sectors, this provides a consistent tailwind for the sector, supporting expansion and operational efficiency.

forces.title: Government capital expenditure supports midstream expansion
forces.description: Higher government capital expenditure, particularly when directed towards infrastructure and energy sectors, stimulates overall economic activity. This directly supports the expansion and utilization of midstream pipeline and storage networks, through increased demand for energy and direct investment in critical infrastructure. This provides a policy-driven tailwind for the sector's growth and development, facilitating new project development and upgrades to existing facilities.

forces.title: Acute negative impact from falling GDP growth on midstream demand
forces.description: India's GDP Annual Growth Rate is currently at 7.8% but exhibits a falling trend (-0.2% change over prior period). This deceleration is leading to a noticeable slowdown in industrial production and transportation volumes across the economy. Consequently, this negative trend is directly impacting demand for midstream services, including pipelines and storage, as overall economic activity and associated energy consumption decrease. This represents an acute, negative cyclical change for the sector, reducing throughput and revenue prospects.

forces.title: Strategic petroleum reserves project expands storage capacity
forces.description: The Union Budget FY26 allocated Rs. 5,597 crore (US$ 640.46 million) for Phase II of the Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (ISPRL) project. This investment aims to develop two vast underground caverns into petroleum storage facilities. This initiative directly expands the storage terminal infrastructure within the midstream sector, enhancing India's energy security and providing a structural increase in storage capacity, which will support future crude oil and product handling volumes and potentially create new revenue streams for midstream players involved in operation and maintenance.
forces.source_title: Oil And Gas Industry In India

viewpoints.title: India's crude sourcing agility tested by compounded geopolitical and tariff disruptions
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings acknowledges India's proven agility in redirecting crude oil sourcing, evidenced by the rapid shift from West Asian to Russian barrels following the Strait of Hormuz closure. However, the firm expresses caution regarding the system's ability to withstand a combined shock of tariff-driven constraints on Russian crude purchases and sustained chokepoint disruptions. This untested scenario, if it materializes, poses a significant risk to the entire oil economy, including the midstream sector's ability to adapt to complex, simultaneous supply chain challenges, moving beyond singular physical route failures.
viewpoints.source_title: Crude Oil at the Geo-political Crossroads

viewpoints.title: India's LNG dependence creates structural midstream vulnerability to geopolitical shocks
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights India's significant structural exposure to external energy shocks, particularly LNG flow disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz, which directly impacts the midstream sector. With 50% of LNG demand met by Gulf imports, geopolitical tensions rapidly cascade into domestic LNG price surges, strained reserves, and reported distribution delays for commercial users via the gas transmission network. This vulnerability underscores the strategic fragility of India's energy and fertiliser systems, emphasizing the need for diversification beyond short-term stabilization measures to enhance midstream resilience.
viewpoints.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

viewpoints.title: India's crude import diversification enhances midstream adaptability amid geopolitical shifts
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings observes India's strategic diversification of crude oil imports, with Russia's share significantly increasing post-FY22 and other sources like Oman and Venezuela gaining prominence. This shift, alongside reduced reliance on traditional West Asian suppliers, demonstrates India's ability to adapt its crude sourcing in response to geopolitical disruptions. For the midstream sector, this indicates a proven capacity to manage changing import origins, re-route shipping, and adjust pipeline and storage logistics, thereby enhancing the overall adaptability and resilience of the crude oil supply chain.

demand_drivers.description: Rapid economic expansion drives industrial and commercial activity, increasing overall energy demand, especially for cleaner fuels like natural gas.
Growing urban centers lead to increased residential and transport sector demand for natural gas, driven by piped gas and CNG vehicles.
Government policies promoting natural gas as a cleaner fuel source encourage its adoption over other fossil fuels across various sectors.
Industrial consumers are expected to account for 40% of India's net demand growth for natural gas, utilizing it as a feedstock and energy source.
Demand from households for piped natural gas (PNG), transport for compressed natural gas (CNG), and power generation contributes significantly to overall gas consumption.
